items.title: Favourable Conditions Begin: Superior and Lesser, and the First of Twelve

items.zh: 何等名為涅槃法緣，而言闕故、無故、不會遇故，不般涅槃？答：有二種緣。何等為二？一、勝，二、劣。云何勝緣？謂正法增上他音，及內如理作意。云何劣緣？謂此劣緣乃有多種。謂若自圓滿、若他圓滿、若善法欲、若正出家、若戒律儀、若根律儀、若於食知量、若初夜後夜常勤修習覺寤瑜伽、若正知而住、若樂遠離、若清淨諸蓋、若依三摩地。云何自圓滿？謂善得人身，生於聖處，諸根無缺，勝處淨信，離諸業障。云何名為善得人身？謂如有一，生人同分，得丈夫身，男根成就；或得女身。如是名為善得人身。
items.en: What is called the condition for the dharma of nirvāṇa? …Answer: There are two kinds of condition. What are the two? Superior, and lesser. What is the superior condition? It is the excellent sound of the true Dharma from another, together with correct attention arising within. What is the lesser condition? This lesser condition is, in fact, of many kinds — namely, one's own perfection, the perfection of others, and so on. …What is one's own perfection? It is: a good human birth, birth in a noble place, unimpaired faculties, pure faith regarding what is excellent, and freedom from karmic obstructions. What is called a good human birth? It is like one who is born within the human category, obtaining a man's body with the male faculty complete, or obtaining a woman's body. This is called a good human birth.

items.title: Self-Perfection Completes: Sound Faculties, Genuine Faith, and Freedom From the Gravest Karma

items.zh: 云何名為生於聖處？謂如有一，生於中國，廣說如前，乃至善士皆往遊涉。如是名為生於聖處。云何名為諸根無缺？謂如有一，性不愚鈍，亦不頑騃，又不瘖瘂，乃至廣說支節無減。彼由如是支節無缺、耳無缺等、能於善品精勤修集。如是名為諸根無缺。云何名為勝處淨信？謂如有一，於諸如來正覺所說法毘奈耶，得淨信心，如是名為勝處淨信。言勝處者，謂諸如來正覺所說法毘奈耶，能生一切世出世間白淨法故。此中所起前行增上諸清淨信，名勝處淨信，能除一切所有煩惱垢穢濁故。云何名為離諸業障？謂能遠離五無間業。所謂於彼害母、害父、害阿羅漢、破和合僧、於如來所惡心出血。隨一所有無間業障，於現法中不作不行，如是名為離諸業障。若有於此五無間業造作增長，於現法中竟不能轉、得般涅槃、生起聖道。故約彼說離諸業障。唯由如是五種支分，自體圓滿。是故說此名自圓滿。
items.en: What is called unimpaired faculties? It is like one who is by nature neither dull-witted, nor stupid, nor mute — and so on at length, down to being free of any missing limb. …What is called pure faith regarding what is excellent? It is like one who attains a pure faith in the Dharma and discipline taught by the fully awakened tathāgatas. This is called pure faith regarding what is excellent. …What is called freedom from karmic obstructions? It is the ability to avoid the five acts of immediate retribution — namely, killing one's mother, killing one's father, killing an arhat, causing schism in the harmonious community, and, with malicious intent, drawing a tathāgata's blood. …It is solely by means of these five components that one's own being is perfected — this, therefore, is called one's own perfection.

items.title: The Second Favourable Condition Opens: What Others Must Supply

items.zh: 云何他圓滿？謂諸佛出世，說正法教，法教久住，法住隨轉，他所哀愍。云何名為諸佛出世？謂如有一，普於一切諸有情類、起善利益增上意樂，修習多千難行苦行，經三大劫阿僧企耶，積集廣大福德、智慧二種資糧；獲得最後上妙之身，安坐無上勝菩提座，斷除五蓋，於四念住善住其心，修三十七菩提分法，現證無上正等菩提。如是名為諸佛出世。過去、未來、現在諸佛，皆由如是名為出世。
items.en: What is perfection supplied by others? It is: buddhas appearing in the world; the teaching of the true Dharma; the true teaching abiding long in the world; the true teaching continuing to be transmitted; and being shown compassion by others. What is called a buddha appearing in the world? It is like one who, giving rise to a supremely powerful intention to benefit all beings without exception, cultivates many thousands of difficult practices and austerities, and, over three great incalculable eons, gathers the vast twin provisions of merit and wisdom, thereby attaining the final, most excellent body, sitting upon the unsurpassed seat of awakening, cutting off the five hindrances, settling the mind well in the four applications of mindfulness, cultivating the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, and directly realising unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening. This is called a buddha appearing in the world. All buddhas — past, future, and present — are called "appearing in the world" for this same reason.

items.title: Teaching the True Dharma: The Twelvefold Body of Scripture

items.zh: 云何名為說正法教？謂即如是諸佛世尊出現於世，哀愍一切諸聲聞故，依四聖諦，宣說真實苦集滅道無量法教。所謂契經、應頌、記別、諷誦、自說、因緣、譬喻、本事、本生、方廣、希法、論議。如是名為說正法教。諸佛世尊及聖弟子，一切正士皆乘此法而得出離，然後為他宣說稱讚，是故說此名為正法。宣說此故，名正法教。
items.en: What is called the teaching of the true Dharma? It is precisely that these buddha-bhagavats, having appeared in the world, out of compassion for all their hearer-disciples, teach — resting on the four noble truths — the true and boundless doctrine of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Namely: discourses, verses that restate what has been said, predictions of future attainment, spontaneous verses, unprompted teachings, teachings prompted by an occasion, parables, accounts of disciples' past lives, accounts of the Buddha's own past lives, teachings of vast scope, accounts of wondrous and rare qualities, and structured treatises. …The buddha-bhagavats, their noble disciples, and all persons of genuine integrity, all attain liberation by relying on this very Dharma, and then, for the sake of others, teach and praise it — it is for this reason that it is called the true Dharma. Teaching it is what is meant by "the teaching of the true Dharma."

items.title: The Teaching Enduring Long: Genuine Attainment vs. Its Many Counterfeits

items.zh: 云何名為法教久住？謂說正法已，轉法輪已，乃至世尊壽量久住，及涅槃後。經爾所時，正行未減、正法未隱，如是名為正法久住。如是久住，當知說彼勝義正法作證道理。
items.en: What is called the teaching abiding long in the world? It is that, once the true Dharma has been taught and the wheel of the Dharma has been turned — whether during the Bhagavat's own lifetime, or after his final nirvāṇa — for however long a span of time, genuine practice has not yet ceased, and the true teaching has not yet vanished: this is called the true Dharma abiding long. …This "abiding long" should be understood as referring to the principle of directly realising the ultimate true Dharma.

items.title: Passing the Torch, and the Compassion of Those Who Provide

items.zh: 云何名為法住隨轉？謂即如是證正法者，了知有力能證如是正法眾生，即如所證，隨轉隨順教授教誡。如是名為法住隨轉。云何名為他所哀愍？
items.en: What is called the true teaching continuing to be transmitted? It is that those who have thus realised the true Dharma, recognising beings who have the capacity to likewise realise this true Dharma, transmit it — exactly as they themselves realised it — through instruction and admonition offered in accordance with it. This is called the true teaching continuing to be transmitted. What is called being shown compassion by others?

blocks.text: What enables the seed to bear fruit? A superior condition and twelve lesser ones. Today: the first ten of the twelve.

The **superior condition** is "the excellent sound of the true Dharma from another, together with correct attention arising within". Master Cháng Bǎi: it is the staple food; the lesser conditions are secondary, but must be complete too.

Five conditions come from oneself: a human birth; birth in a noble land; sound faculties; pure faith in what is excellent; and freedom from karmic obstruction. Master Cháng Bǎi notices that the text skips the eyes and names the ears first: "the most important thing in learning the Dharma is hearing it."

Five come from others: **Buddhas appear** (after gathering merit and wisdom over three incalculable aeons); the **true Dharma is taught**; it **endures**; it **continues to be transmitted**; and **others provide support** out of compassion.

The teaching is the **twelvefold scripture**: discourses, restating verses, predictions, independent verses, inspired utterances, occasions, parables, past events, birth stories, extensive teachings, marvels, and analyses. Master Cháng Bǎi: occasions belong to the Vinaya, analyses to the Abhidharma, the rest to the sūtras.

"For however long genuine practice has not ceased, and the true teaching has not vanished, the true Dharma abides." Master Cháng Bǎi: at first the Dharma is like milk; later water is added, and with enough water it is no longer pure. Hence the treatise contrasts genuine attainment with its counterfeits.
"Transmission" means passing the realised Dharma from one mind to another so that it continues. The last condition, support from others, is the compassion of benefactors who provide robes and food.

quiz.q: What does the treatise say is the superior condition for the dharma of nirvāṇa?
options: the excellent sound of the true Dharma from another, and correct attention within
quiz.why: "What is the superior condition? It is the excellent sound of the true Dharma from another, together with correct attention arising within." Master Cháng Bǎi: the main conditions are "superior," the secondary "lesser" — both must be complete.

quiz.q: If the lesser conditions are "lesser," are they still needed? What do the masters say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: superior conditions are the staple, lesser ones the side dishes — both needed; Miào Jìng: though lesser, they must be complete
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the superior condition is the staple food, the main thing; the lesser conditions are secondary, but they too must be complete. Venerable Miào Jìng: together these are the lesser conditions — though lesser, they must be fulfilled.

quiz.q: Why does "unimpaired faculties" stress hearing rather than sight first, per the masters?
options: the most important thing in learning the Dharma is hearing it; a good teacher's instruction matters most
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it doesn't mention the eyes but goes straight to the ears, because the most important thing in learning the Dharma is hearing it. Venerable Miào Jìng: the six faculties should begin with the eye, but here the ear comes first — showing how important a good teacher's instruction is.

quiz.q: What are the five components of perfection supplied by others?
options: buddhas appearing, the true Dharma taught, the teaching abiding long, the teaching transmitted, compassion from others
the five aggregates of the Dharma body
quiz.why: "Buddhas appearing in the world; the teaching of the true Dharma; the true teaching abiding long; the true teaching continuing to be transmitted; and being shown compassion by others." Master Cháng Bǎi: a buddha's presence is the best; without one, the Dharma and someone to teach it must still be present.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi distribute the twelve divisions among the three baskets?
options: occasions belong to the vinaya, structured treatises to the abhidharma, and the other ten to the sutras
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: occasions (nidāna) belong to the vinaya, structured treatises to the abhidharma, and the other ten belong to the sutras. Precepts were established on specific occasions, so occasions belong to the vinaya.

quiz.q: What does the treatise call "the teaching abiding long"?
options: after the teaching and turning of the wheel, during the Buddha's life and after, genuine practice has not ceased and the true teaching not vanished
quiz.why: "For however long a span of time, genuine practice has not yet ceased, and the true teaching has not yet vanished: this is called the true Dharma abiding long." Master Cháng Bǎi: both the teaching and its practice still exist in the world.

quiz.q: What image does Master Cháng Bǎi use for the Dharma gradually losing purity?
options: the Dharma begins as milk; in the end much water may be added and it is no longer pure
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the Dharma at first is milk; at the end water may be added, and with much water it is no longer pure. Hence the treatise distinguishes genuine realisation from its counterfeits.
